_provenance.notes: The North Pacific Anadromous Fish Commission (NPAFC) was established by the Convention for the Conservation of Anadromous Stocks in the North Pacific Ocean (1992), which prohibits directed high seas salmon fishing beyond 200-mile EEZs. Members: US, Russia, Japan, Canada, South Korea. Before NPAFC, Japan, South Korea, and the Soviet Union conducted major high seas driftnet salmon fisheries. The 1993 closure of these fisheries was a major conservation gain for Alaska salmon. NPAFC now coordinates research and monitoring.
